subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a temp artifact provenance and cleanup model, and which parts should instead live in plugins, SDK seams, or ClawHub?
rationale: The safety goal fits current priorities, but implementing the request touches storage policy, cleanup authority, agent/tool APIs, doctor/runtime guardrails, and core-vs-plugin boundaries that need maintainer intent before a safe repair can be queued.

options.title: Core guardrails plus plugin seam
options.body: Have core cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, leaving workflow-specific classifications such as audit/review staging to plugins or ClawHub packages.

options.title: Full core provenance registry
options.body: Build a core-owned temp artifact registry and cleanup/janitor policy for all first-class OpenClaw temp artifacts, accepting broader storage and cleanup responsibility in core.

options.title: Close broad core scope
options.body: Decline the broad core default and keep only concrete bug reports such as backup stale-temp cleanup plus plugin/community implementations for workflow janitors.

recommendation.title: Core guardrails plus plugin seam
recommendation.body: Have core cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, leaving workflow-specific classifications such as audit/review staging to plugins or ClawHub packages.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest combination of recent temp-boundary history, product-scope review context, and prior related ClawHub decision evidence.
